headline: This law extends federal fire grant programs through 2024 and adds rules on training, grant uses, and oversight for firefighters and emergency responders.
what_it_does: The law renews three federal grant programs for firefighters and fire prevention through fiscal year 2024: the Assistance to Firefighters Grants, the Fire Prevention and Safety Grants, and the SAFER staffing grants. It lets money from the Assistance to Firefighters Grants pay for training on how to recognize and respond to people with mental illness, instead of using SAFER funds. It also allows SAFER grants to help convert part-time or paid-on-call firefighters into full-time firefighters. Finally, it lets the U.S. Fire Administration create online training on managing these grants and requires a grant oversight system to reduce fraud, waste, and mismanagement.

who_it_affects.how: They may receive federal grants for mental-health crisis training and, through SAFER, for staffing changes.
Fire departments may use SAFER grants to convert these positions into full-time jobs.
The required online training must be accessible to volunteer and other non-career responders, and it must fit their time and cost limits.

who_it_affects.group: Local fire departments applying for federal grants
who_it_affects.how: They can keep applying for these three grant programs through 2024 and must follow the new grant oversight framework.

when_it_takes_effect: Enacted January 3, 2018, with the grant programs authorized through fiscal year 2024.
